Lead Story · The Holiday Season

The Holidays Arrive at the Triton: Art Fair, Mixer & a Night in “Tritonville”

Three dates anchor the season — a beloved art fair with 25–30 local makers, a chamber holiday mixer among the galleries, and a members-only appreciation night to close the year.

From the Triton Museum of Art BuddySanta Clara — Nov. 14, 2026

The museum's holiday season opens in earnest on Saturday, November 21, when the Triton Holiday Art Fair fills the galleries indoors from 10 AM to 4 PM. Shoppers can browse 25–30 local artist vendors and small businesses, hear live Victorian carolers performing traditional Christmas songs, and pick up baked goods — with free entry throughout the day.

The celebrations continue into December. On Wednesday, December 2, the Silicon Valley Chamber brings its “Holiday Extravaganza” mixer to the museum for an evening gathering among the exhibitions — registration is required. Then, on Friday, December 11, from 6 to 8 PM, the museum thanks its supporters with “Tritonville,” a Members Appreciation Event that is free for members and invite-only, with RSVP by invitation.

All five current exhibitions remain on view through the holidays (see below), making any of these evenings — or a quiet weekday morning — a good excuse for a visit. Admission and parking are always free.

Sat Nov 21 · 10 AM–4 PM

Triton Holiday Art Fair

25–30 local artist vendors, Victorian carolers and baked goods, indoors at the museum. Free entry.

Wed Dec 2 · Evening

Now on View

Five exhibitions · All free

Eye/Hand

Harry Clewans

Aug 29, 2026 – Jan 3, 2027

Mosaic-like compositions built from hundreds of the artist's own woodcut prints of found and decayed objects, assembled on wood panels.

Rose Sellery: Fragile Strength

Rose Sellery · Permanent Collection Gallery

Aug 29, 2026 – Jan 3, 2027

Sculpture, conceptual garments and photography made from everyday materials — fragility recast as strength, with humor and irony.

🎤 Artist talk & tour: Sat Dec 5, 1 PM — see calendar

-futility in three acts-

Sieglinde Van Damme

Aug 29, 2026 – Jan 10, 2027

Three rotating video works on identity and immigration. The current act, “v o i d,” runs to Nov 18; the final act, “Things change and then nothing happens,” opens Nov 19.

Intrusive Thoughts

Devon Blood · Cowell Room Gallery

Aug 15, 2026 – Jan 17, 2027

Raw, personal paintings — including acrylic on black velvet — shaped by the artist's life with OCD. His charge to viewers: “stay up, stay strong, keep laughing.”

Here and There

Tim Guan

Aug 22, 2026 – Jan 17, 2027

Figurative oils reflecting on innovation culture — and the slower work of genuine human connection.

Around the Museum

A Family Connection

Mei-Ying Dell'Aquila, Trustee & Teacher

Mei-Ying Dell'Aquila — a Trustee and Treasurer of the museum — teaches the January 30 “Year of the Ram” ink-painting workshops for children, teens and adults.

Coming in January

Fifty Years of Mitchell Johnson

Mitchell Johnson: Fifty Years of Painting opens January 16, 2027 — a retrospective already featured in WSJ Magazine. Also opening Jan 16: Bassett/Bradford: In Conversation. On Jan 30: Beyond the Visible (Trung Cao) and The Burdens of Memory (Mishaal Atheer).

The Salon at the Triton

Best of Show: Rachel Davis

The 2026 Salon's Best of Show was Rachel Davis — the award earns her a solo show at the museum in 2027.

Since 1965

Santa Clara County's Oldest

Founded in 1965, the Triton is the oldest non-university museum in Santa Clara County, collecting and exhibiting contemporary and historical work with an emphasis on Greater Bay Area artists.
